name: Java
summary: The most widely employed language in the corporate world: strong typing, object orientation done properly and thirty years of compatibility.
prerequisites: None. This course teaches the language from scratch — it is the entry point for anyone who has never written Java.
syllabus: The JVM, the life of a program and the syntax of the language
Types, casting, strings, arrays and control flow
Full object orientation: classes, inheritance, interfaces and encapsulation
Records, enums, nested classes and packages
Collections and generics: picking the right structure
Exceptions, annotations and the module system
topics: The JVM: compilation, bytecode, execution and LTS releases
The life of a program: from source file to process
Basic syntax, conventions and the first program
Primitive types, wrappers and `var`
Variables, scope and lifetime
Type conversion: implicit, explicit and loss of precision
Strings and their methods: immutability, `StringBuilder` and formatting
Maths operations, `Math` and floating-point pitfalls
Arrays: declaration, traversal and multidimensional arrays
Conditionals: `if`, `switch` and switch expressions
Loops: `for`, `while`, `do-while` and `for-each`
Classes and objects: what exists at runtime
Fields and methods: state and behaviour
Access modifiers and why `private` is the sensible default
The `static` keyword: when something belongs to the class, not the object
The `final` keyword on variables, methods and classes
Nested, inner and anonymous classes
Packages, imports and project organisation
Object lifecycle: construction, reference and garbage collection
Inheritance: reuse, `super` and the limits of a hierarchy
Abstraction: the abstract class and the contract it imposes
Encapsulation: why an accessor is not red tape
Interfaces, default methods and multiple inheritance of behaviour
Method overloading and overriding: the difference that trips people up
Static and dynamic binding: who decides which method runs
Method chaining and the fluent interface
Initialiser blocks and initialisation order
`enum`: more than a constant, a type with behaviour
`record`: immutable data without ceremony
Pass by value: the most common misunderstanding in Java
Collections: array versus `ArrayList`, and when each one fits
`List`, `Set` and `Map`: choosing the right implementation
`Queue`, `Deque` and `Stack`
`Iterator` and safe traversal while modifying
Generics: typed collections, wildcards and type erasure
Checked and unchecked exceptions: `try`, `catch`, `finally`
`try-with-resources` and automatic closing
Writing your own exception and the `Throwable` hierarchy
Annotations: the language ones, the framework ones and your own
The module system (JPMS): `module-info` and strong encapsulation
